1088/0031-9155/61/9/3500 Abstract The combination of positron emission tomography (PET) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as a multi-modal imaging technique is considered Paper very promising and powerful with regard to in vivo disease progression examination, therapy response monitoring and drug development
However, PET–MRI system design enabling simultaneous operation with unaffected 0031-9155 intrinsic performance of both modalities is challenging

As one of the major issues, both the PET detectors and the MRI radio-frequency (RF) subsystem 3500 are exposed to electromagnetic (EM) interference, which may lead to PET and MRI signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) deteriorations

Early digitization of electronic PET signals within the MRI bore helps to preserve PET SNR, 3526 but occurs at the expense of increased amount of PET electronics inside the MRI and associated RF field emissions

This raises the likelihood of PET-related MRI interference by coupling into the MRI RF coil unwanted 9 spurious signals considered as RF noise, as it degrades MRI SNR and results in MR image artefacts

In this paper, we present RF interference reduction methods which rely on EM field coupling–decoupling principles of RF receive coils rather than suppressing emitted fields

We present simulations and magnetic-field map scans visualising the impact of altered clock phase pattern on the spatial RF field distribution, followed by MRI noise and SNR scans performed with an operating PET module using different clock frequencies and phase patterns
In this paper, we present initial investigations of techniques which aim at the modification of the PET electronics’ RF field emission

Our results obtained with frequencies of 100 MHz and 160 MHz clearly demonstrate that well chosen frequencies help to reduce PET-related RF noise, or in other words increase the RF silence of our PET detector
